## Sitting 1 — plan & sky trials (scratch, cold-press seed 3117, 1056x704)
Subject: low-tide estuary at evening. Graded sky (blue-gray top -> rose -> warm glow at horizon ~y340), low distant headland, granulating mudflats with an S-channel reflecting sky light, a beached boat, receding posts.

Sky trials:
- T1 FAIL: 12uL drop grid then 196 segment strokes (40-cell, width70, top-up to 5uL, 0.5 ultramarine per 5uL) -> navy, far too dark; 6.3s to lay, lower rows striped because pre-wet had dried.
- T2 FAIL: b:wash bands: ~4s per 90-cell band -> too slow; stripes; pigment piled at band boundaries.
- T3 FAIL: one full-width stroke per row (30uL, duration 0.25): brush emptied in first ~200 cells -> pale middle. Hypothesis: release is front-loaded; long rows need top-ups.
- T4 GOOD: drop grid 10uL r85 (spacing 118x90) over sky; rows every 40 cells, width70, 62-cell segments, duration 0.012 each, top-up to 5uL with pigment proportional (per uL: ultramarine 0.032*(1-t)^1.3, rose 0.008 gaussian at t=.62, raw sienna+qbo ~0.01 near horizon, burnt sienna .003 upper). 9 rows in 1.94s; smooth gradation, no stripes. Damp at ~5s, dry ~7s. Pigment collects slightly at bottom boundary.
- Clouds charged at 2.0-2.4s: width40, 3uL + ultra .10/bs .04/rose .02 per stroke -> soft-edged gray-violet blobs, short (brush runs out ~150 cells).

## Finish / handoff (t~357s)
Title: "Low Water, Evening Channel". Final state dry.
Last steps: restored boat strake (cad red 1.2/cad orange .3/bs .2 per uL x1.8, 6 rows width4, 0.5uL) over the darkened hull -> bright again; buff+naples rail; interior sliver naples/ochre/buff with two shade lines (bu .9/rs .5 per uL) -> reads as open boat with ribs. Samphire dabs (width5, bs/alizarin/raw sienna ~1u/uL) on the ragged bank top; light opaque grass tufts (naples 2/raw sienna 1/buff 1 per uL, width2-2.6) over the dark foreground read well against dark — unlike opaque streaks on mud, vertical lit blades work. Three gulls (paynes gray 2/bu .8 per uL, width2.4, 2 strokes each) in the glow. Signature "C" at (960,688) in sepia — nearly invisible on the dark mud.

Unresolved passages:
- Mid-distance mud on the left still shows the stacked horizontal "brick" rows; sandbars helped but it's somewhat schematic.
- Dark foreground band reads heavy and has faint horizontal stripes from glaze rows; its ragged top is an accident accepted as a vegetation bank.
- Headland treeline is a rather even palisade; tall crowns are small.
- Channel lower water is flat lavender; ripples barely read. No reflection of posts/boat in water.
- Sky clouds are horizontal lozenges, a bit uniform in shape.

Practical lessons (hypotheses unless noted):
- Value concentration: small dark marks need 1–3 pigment units per uL; washes 0.02–0.06 per uL. Concentration, not volume, drives darkness (observed on scratch).
- Long wet rows: top up every 30–60 cells to a fixed load; single long loaded strokes empty early (observed).
- Pre-wet drop grids + many rows over large dry painted areas can flood and migrate ~100 cells beyond the strokes, drying with cauliflower edges (observed once on painting; scratch trial didn't reproduce — condition difference unknown, maybe the painting had more surrounding glazes/less absorbency or more total water). Keep pre-wet away from finished focal objects.
- Opaque light streaks (buff titanium) on dark mud = collage look; opaque lights work as thin vertical grass and boat rail (observed).
- Cadmium red over dark dried paint stays bright (observed); indian red reads salmon/chalky.
- Stacked fading rows from a crisp top line make convincing mud ridges/sandbars (observed).
